result.note: Tests the Aravalli engine deal: SAFHAL joint venture, power class and the Mi-17 replacement role of the Indian Multi-Role Helicopter.

questions.prompt: In August 2026, Hindustan Aeronautics (HAL) and France's Safran Helicopter Engines signed to co-develop the 'Aravalli' engine for the Indian Multi-Role Helicopter. Consider the following statements about this engine:
items: It is being co-developed through the SAFHAL joint venture.
The helicopter it will power is meant to replace the Russian Mi-17 helicopters in use.
It falls in the 1,500 to 2,000 shaft-horsepower class.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong: the Aravalli engine is in the 3,500 to 4,000 shaft-horsepower class. The deal covers design, manufacture and lifecycle support for the engine of the under-development 13-tonne Indian Multi-Role Helicopter.
questions.source: The engine covers design, manufacture, and lifecycle support in the 3,500 to 4,000 shaft-horsepower class, and would power a domestic replacement for the Russian Mi-17 helicopters currently in use.
